div.head: Hn 11.5
div.ab: Qui uxoratus faciet adulterium, habeat rex (uel dominus) superiorem, episcopus inferiorem.

note.label: same wording
note.quote: ‘the king have the upper and the bishop the lower’. That was also the wording of Leges Henrici Primi, as applied to cases of adultery

div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 557 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: EGu. punishes incestuous persons thus. Cf. 21<sup>r</sup>. 73, 6a
u. d. vom Corr. übergeschr. Sc, im Text übrige
u. d. written above by the corrector Sc, in the text the rest
eius fügt zu und zwar zu rex Sc Hg; ei. u. d. Wh; doch bezog es Verf. oder Interpolator auf dom.
eius added, and indeed attached to rex, by Sc Hg; ei. u. d. Wh; but the author or interpolator referred it to dom.

Vgl. Gl Ehebruch 13. Heinrich I. strafte mit Geld sogar Kleriker-Konkubinat.—Am Rande später: Item habeat rex similiter cum episcopo emendas de adulterio.—Zu 11, 6 am Rande später: Item de periurio commisso—11, 7 helfeng{16}—11, 9 reus{20} sit et c. d., n. deneg., am Rande spät: Quod confessio non negetur reo illam petenti—11, 10 helfeng{22}—11, 11 laslith{24}—11, 11a. Si a. illic u., hoc emendat{29}—11, 12 laslith{36}—11, 13a Et si intra u. a. s. ma. ca.{38}, p. morāgyuam—11, 13b maritus{42} eius w.—11, 14 ini., ei reddat{44} ad—11, 14a om. c. n.{46} Rs

Cf. Gl Ehebruch 13. Henry I punished even clerical concubinage with money payments.—In the margin, later: Item habeat rex similiter cum episcopo emendas de adulterio.—On 11, 6 in the margin, later: Item de periurio commisso—11, 7 helfeng{16}—11, 9 reus{20} sit et c. d., n. deneg., in the margin, late: Quod confessio non negetur reo illam petenti—11, 10 helfeng{22}—11, 11 laslith{24}—11, 11a.
